goal: Replace the hardcoded domain-agent roster with a real permission-driven mechanism: a user participating in a Dialog can enable the lead agent of any OTHER domain where they hold real Admin-level DomainPermission -- starting with Ceox, Chuck's own agent, becoming addable to ke3p's cast through the Cast Header. This is infrastructure -- real per-agent delegation is deliberately a separate, later phase.
done_when: A real backend capability resolves, for the current authenticated user, every domain where they hold Admin-level DomainPermission (or are Domain.ownerId) -- and for each, resolves that domain's real lead agent (reuse the existing resolveDomainLeadContext / loadDomainScopedAgents pattern, do not reinvent lead resolution)

Those agents are surfaced as addable candidates via a real 'Add' action in DirectorCastHeader -- clicking it shows the candidate list (e.g. 'Ceox -- from [Chuck's domain]'), selecting one enables that agent for the CURRENT dialog

The enablement persists for that Dialog (survives reload) -- Cursor decides and documents the storage shape (a new field/array on Dialog, or a join table; review whether the existing CrossDomainShare model's contentType/contentId pattern fits before inventing something new -- it may not, since it's approval-gated domain-to-domain sharing and this is user-permission-driven, not domain-to-domain -- document the reasoning either way)
Once enabled, the agent renders through the exact same BoardInstrumentsBar/DirectorCastHeader machinery already shipped -- no new chip component, no new invocation UI

Strict security boundary: an agent is only addable if the CURRENT user genuinely holds Admin-level DomainPermission (or ownership) on that agent's home domain, checked at request time, not cached client-side or trusted from the frontend -- this is the one hard non-negotiable in this handoff

The existing hardcoded DOMAIN_ACCESSIBLE_PLATFORM_AGENT_SLUGS = ['cloud','rendr'] stays as the platform baseline every domain still gets automatically -- this handoff is additive (a domain can gain MORE agents via user permission), it does not remove or replace the baseline
pnpm run quick:web and pnpm run quick:api pass

Manual check: on ke3p (Chuck as Admin), the Cast Header's Add action surfaces Ceox as a real candidate (from Chuck's own domain where Ceox is lead), enabling it makes Ceox appear and persist as a cast member on reload

a new backend endpoint for resolving a user's cross-domain-admin addable agents and for enabling/persisting one onto a Dialog
apps/web/src/v0/boards/UniversalConversation.tsx (wire the enabled-agent list into the existing instrument list alongside the hardcoded baseline)

pattern_ref: Chuck's own framing, verbatim: 'a User that is involved in a dialog is able to enable lead agents from any domain they themselves have Admin privilege over.' DomainPermission.role already carries admin/user roles per domain -- use it directly, don't build a parallel permission system. resolveDomainLeadContext (apps/web/src/v0/lib/domainLeadAgent.ts) and loadDomainScopedAgents.ts already resolve 'this domain's lead agent' correctly -- reuse that resolution for the OTHER domain, don't reimplement it. CrossDomainShare exists in schema but is approval-gated domain-to-domain content sharing -- check whether it fits before assuming it does; this feature is user-permission-driven, which is a different shape.

context.phase: Follow-on to realm-header-cast-and-multiselect (archived, shipped). Chuck tested the shipped multi-select live and found two real gaps underneath it: no real delegation, and no real cast-membership mechanism -- cast is entirely hardcoded (DOMAIN_ACCESSIBLE_PLATFORM_AGENT_SLUGS = ['cloud','rendr']) with no way for a domain to gain a new agent without a code change.
related_handoffs: director-lead-initiated-delegation (queued, deliberately NOT started -- see notes)
context.notes: Two-phase plan, both scoped now so nothing shows up as a surprise later, but deliberately sequenced -- Chuck's own explicit direction: get this infrastructure right first, treat real delegation as a separate, later, more careful piece of work because of token-cost implications. Phase 2 (director-lead-initiated-delegation, not yet a handoff file, described here for continuity): the LEAD agent (not the user directly, and not an automatic multi-call-everyone-every-turn model) decides whether and which enabled cast agents to consult for a given reply; when consulted, their contribution should be deliberately minimal/collapsed feedback, not a full independent completion -- this matches the already-designed 'chorus' shape in docs/universal-board-dialog-orchestration.md (collapsed beats under the Lead's reply, not full agent swaps). Explicit design constraint carried from Chuck directly: do not build something that multiplies LLM calls linearly with cast size by default -- the whole point of 'minimal feedback' is bounding token cost, not maximizing agent participation. Do not start Phase 2 until Phase 1 (this handoff) is shipped and verified.
